_comment: Cycle-charge stance demo (seed 12345): box-select the player's two cavalry regiments (right of the line, ~x 1027 and 1356, front ranks on the y=300 line, cavalry centres at y -180), press J to arm the Cycle charge stance, then right-click the enemy Infantry regiment at (291,723). The horse charges in, lands its momentum hit, then peels back to a standoff and charges AGAIN -- the caracole loop -- instead of grinding in melee once the charge bonus is spent. The HUD flashes 'Cycle charge' when J is pressed and the order cursor turns violet.

overlap.reason: Measured by tools/check.sh demo_defects on this tree, front-on-line deployment. uid1 (the player Infantry, pressed by the enemy foot) dips to nnd_min 1.56 wu against its 2.25 wu floor: transient press compression. uid8 (team 1's deep cavalry, 9 ranks) is under a continuous AI ATTACK order whose target re-selects mid-clip, and each retarget re-rotates the block before it has re-squared, compressing its own files: 2.97 wu against the 5.0 wu floor, the mechanism main already exempted for uid8 and #1546 tracks. uid3 (the player's charging cavalry) dips to nnd_min 3.48 wu against the 5.0 wu floor at tick 1294, in the 2-tick dense samples after the tick-1122 divergence. That reading is new with the row-major casualty close-up: the merge-base e81ea9fa passes at 6.49 wu. In the charge turnaround mounts 33 and 47, each about 150 wu off his slot, swap sides across each other on both trees; the close-up's different pairing after uid3's casualty brings them closer as they pass. #1804 tracks the swap. uid9 (14.5 wu) no longer needs the exemption.

path_crossing.reason: Charging cavalry paths cross during the cycle-charge breakthrough, disengagement wheel, and realignment: in the turnaround mounts about 150 wu off their slots swap sides across each other (#1804).

shape_residual.reason: uid4 (the player's 80-horse caracole cavalry) keeps a growing shape residual after its charge contact, tracked in #1820. The contact snaps that scatter it are the same on main 9d39a353 and on #1806's branch, and the residual rises identically through tick 1200 (24.6 wu on main, 24.9 on the branch, 4-tick samples). On main the troop re-contacts by about tick 1176-1200, so its later samples are masked as contact; it reaches 65.1 wu at tick 1296, and 2-tick scans fail the metric there too. On the branch a hasty march's grid lag keeps its men nearer their slots after the contact, the anchor takes a different line and the troop does not re-contact, so the clip's own ticks judge it: 104.3 wu against the 30 wu threshold (66.5 at tick 1260, 100.3 at 1296).
